summary: Chelan National Forest crow's-nest lookout on Juniper Point, Okanogan County, WA; built 1930s; collapsed about 2007 per two sources; remains in Loomis State Forest.

facts.design: Sawed-off fir topped as a crow's nest, with a small stick platform, a 15-foot ladder and an Osborne firefinder; tent camp nearby
facts.status_note: Reported collapsed about 2007, though a 2015 news report describes the fire-scarred tree still there. Ground remains: tent floor, flagpole, woodpile, food cooler.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Chelan National Forest) per the Register; the site is described as within Loomis State Forest

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb describes a walk from a parking area: cross a small creek, follow an old road, then go above the cliffs to the point. No source found says whether the public may enter.

events.note: Panorama photos taken from the crow's nest
Tree and platform reported collapsed about 2007; exact date not given. A 2015 report describes the fire-scarred tree still there (see resolved_conflicts)
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on November 17, 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and Firelookout say the late 1930s; WillhiteWeb says the mid-1930s. The story gives both and no exact year, so no built event is recorded.
The Register lists the U.S. Forest Service as administrator, but says the site lies within Loomis State Forest. The story reports both and does not settle the current manager.

The Register and WillhiteWeb say the tree collapsed about 2007. A 2015 news report says the fire-scarred tree and firewood were still there. The story reports both and does not resolve the difference.

notes_for_editor: Built year disagrees (late 1930s per the Register and Firelookout, mid-1930s per WillhiteWeb), and the abandonment date is only the early 1940s, so neither gets a dated event. Coordinates conflict: FFLOS 48.86268, -119.75513 vs West US Lookouts 48.8665, -119.7427; not resolved here. No source found says whether the public may enter the site, and no source names a keeper. A Facebook group post (OHfirewatch) says Lonny Gadberry built and manned the site; it could not be read from the cache, so it is not used. The Register and WillhiteWeb both give about 2007 for the collapse. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 2015 report conflicts with the 2007 collapse date; the story reports both. The report says the firewood stack had been tipped over, so the story says only that the firewood was still there.
